title: A first-order Madelung tie-break on the round four-sphere: Kelvin parity, convex order and the Thomas-Fermi field
description: In the Demkov-Ostrovsky model of the Madelung rule, the one-electron levels with equal N=n+l are degenerate at zero energy, and paper 1 showed that the model is the circle-invariant conformal Laplacian of the round four-sphere. The rule's second part, lower n first within a group, is not explained by the model. We prove that within every group the laws of || ( the polar angle) for consecutive l are in strict increasing convex order, with an explicit closed form from Gegenbauer polynomials and the Laguerre inequality (Theorems 1 and 2). It is not first-order dominance: the distribution functions cross. Hence a perturbation of the Tietz field that depends on r alone, with Kelvin-even weakening increasing and convex in ||, splits every group lower n first at first order (Theorem 3, valid near the Tietz field). For the Thomas-Fermi field, whose weakening is not convex at the poles, Theorem 3 is not applied: a direct interval computation of the first-order slopes certifies the splitting in every group with N≤17, relative to its nearest Tietz field (one fitted scale, robust by estimate for 0.40≤ a≤0.65 at N≤8; Corollary 4). A numerical shooting check finds no level crossing inside a group along the whole path from the Tietz to the Thomas-Fermi field for N≤12 (Proposition 5); at the Thomas-Fermi end the groups 11 and 12 already overlap, so only the order inside a group is claimed. We do not derive real atoms, the spin factor or an ordering by zero-energy coupling.
